newsitem.title: ZAIRE: No truce, Mobutu must go, Zaire rebels say.
newsitem.headline: No truce, Mobutu must go, Zaire rebels say.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Wednesday the fall of Zaire's second city Lubumbashi should force ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko to resign and ruled out a ceasefire.

"The fall of Lubumbashi is the total collapse of Mobutu because if Mobutu is intelligent he will realise that he must resign and has no other choice," Louis Nyarubasa, an official in the rebel information department, said in the eastern city of Goma.
Asked whether the rebel alliance would now agree to a ceasefire with Mobutu's forces, he said: "We can't stop the war because he hasn't resigned, so we aren't able to stop."
The rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire led by Laurent Kabila has seized nearly half of Africa's third largest country since revolt in the east began in October.
Rebels entered Lubumbashi on Wednesday to cheers of "Kabila, Kabila" through the southern suburbs from the direction of the Zambian border.

Rebels said they met fierce resistance 15 km (10 miles) out of the city, after which they had marched in. Government troops seemed to have fled towards the airport six km (four miles) to the northeast.
